analysis.investment_thesis: Rikhav Securities screens cheaply on surface metrics (P/E 6.63, P/B ~0.65, low debt), but it is a recently listed small brokerage whose FY25 net profit collapsed 43% (42→24 Cr) and whose operating cash flow has been negative in 3 of the last 4 years. The statistical cheapness is real but the earnings quality and cyclicality do not meet my standard for a defensive margin-of-safety purchase.
key_strengths: P/B of roughly 0.65 (159 Cr mcap vs 244 Cr equity) — below book value
Low leverage: borrowings just 5 Cr against 244 Cr equity; D/E ~0.02
P/E of 6.63 and 4 consecutive years of positive reported earnings
key_risks: Net profit fell from 42 Cr (FY24) to 24 Cr (FY25) despite revenue tripling — margin collapse
Operating cash flow negative in 3 of 4 years (-37, -9, +109, -188 Cr) — reported earnings not converting to cash
Brokerage earnings are highly cyclical to equity market conditions; no through-cycle record visible
red_flags: Recent IPO/listing (BSE code 544340) — short public track record; equity jumped 139→244 Cr largely from issuance, not retained earnings
FY25 OCF of -188 Cr versus reported PAT of +24 Cr — severe divergence
Other income collapsed to zero in FY24-25 after contributing materially earlier
analysis.detailed_analysis:
On my quantitative filters the stock passes several tests: P/E under 10, P/B well under 1.0, debt negligible, and promoter holding a comfortable 64%. At 159 Cr market cap against 244 Cr of book equity, Mr. Market is in effect offering the business at a discount to stated net worth. For a Graham-style net-net hunter this is the headline attraction, and it is not trivial.

However, the deeper numbers give pause. FY25 revenue of 328 Cr produced only 24 Cr of net profit — operating income actually fell from 55 Cr to 34 Cr year-on-year, and free cash flow swung to -189 Cr. A stockbroker whose cash flows oscillate this violently is a leveraged play on market activity, not a stable earning-power franchise. The 3-year earnings CAGR of 10% masks the fact that the most recent year is down sharply. I require several years of stable, proven earning power before paying even a low multiple; this company has perhaps one genuinely strong year (FY24) surrounded by weaker ones. I would wait for either a deeper discount (say, P/B under 0.5) or two to three more years of demonstrated profit stability before committing capital.
